newsitem.title: UK: Unigate trading in line with its forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Unigate trading in line with its forecasts.

text.p: British food and distribution group Unigate Plc said on Tuesday that overall the group continued to perform in line with its expectations and at similar levels to last year.
Unigate said it continues to see growth in its fresh foods and UK logistics supplier Wincanton businesses as they benefit from recent organic investment and acquisitions.

Profits at Wincanton were up from 10.6 million at 12.3 million in the six months to September 30 and the division saw some easing of margin pressure. New business gained with Argos, British Airways, the Greenalls Group and H.J.Heinz contributed to the improved results.
"However, in the highly competitive markets in which we are operating, our Dairy business is being impacted by the weak commodity markets," said the company.
Operating profit from European foods increased 3.1 million to 44.1 million stg, with fresh foods maintaining its strong growth due to the benefit of recent acquisitions and tighter cost control.

Unigate bought Kraft's European margarine and spreads business, which includes the Vitalite and Golden Churn brands, in August. The purchase from Kraft gives Unigate, which already owns Utterley Butterly and St Ivel Gold, a 25 percent share of the British margarines and spreads market.
Unilever, owner of Flora and I Can't Believe It's Not Butter, is the leader with a 44.6 percent share.
Dairy, which now includes the results of the butter and powder activities and the liquid milk business, recorded profits down 2.9 million at 17.6 milion.
Unigate estimated that lower butter and milk powder prices cost it about 4.0 million stg in the first half compared with the same period last year.
Overall sales of liquid milk fell by seven percent on last year due to lower sales at the doorstep. Sales to supermarkets declined by 2.4 percent.
In Butter and Powder, falling commodity prices resulted in lower margins, said the company.

In the half year a total of 100 million stg was spent on acquisitions, including 20 million on the Hargrave pork products business and 79 million on Kraft's Vitalite and Golden Churn businesses to add to St Ivel's brands Gold and Utterly Butter.
Net cash held at September 30, 1996 was 57.9 million.

Unigate exited from the U.S. restaurant business with the sale of Black-eyed Pea for 42 million stg in July and the sale of Taco Bueno and Casa Bonita for 27 million after the half-year end. The sale enabled Unigate to focus on developing its core European food and distribution business.
